title: MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn is a glutinous open pollinated corn variety for Luzon. 101 to 105 days to harvest, 4.5 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn is a glutinous open pollinated corn variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2025 as NSIC 2025 Cn 344. Mariano Marcos State University bred it. It takes 101 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 4.52 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 101 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain.
**Yield:** 4.52 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn takes 101 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is 5.9 days longer than the average of the 19 glutinous open pollinated corn varieties with a day count, 97.1 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 4.52 t/ha trails the average of its group, 5.09. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its ears grew about 14.08 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 78.3 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears.
Where and when to plant MMSU BMIR Glut #5 corn

The registry recommends it for Luzon. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 101 to 105 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 4.52 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.
The registry recommends it for Luzon. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of MMSU BMIR Glut #5?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
